correctness.rationale: Under the literal ambient-field reading, an element primitive in \(\mathbb F_{p^{ln}}\) has multiplicative order \(p^{ln}-1\), so no nontrivial \(p^d\)-Frobenius with \(d<ln\) can fix it; its complete \(p\)-Frobenius orbit therefore has \(ln\) distinct elements. A basis consisting of that full orbit forces \(D(1,b)\) to have ambient dimension \(ln\), hence to equal \(\mathbb F_{q^n}\). Conversely the primitive normal basis theorem gives such a basis for the full ambient field. The explicit \((q,n)=(4,3)\) witness was independently recomputed in \(\mathbb F_2[g]/(g^6+g+1)\): \(g\) has order 63, \(b=g^{34}\), \(1+b=g^{31}\) lie in the same nontrivial Dickson coset, and the distributivity equation has exactly the four roots of \(d^4=d\), i.e. \(\mathbb F_4\), containing no ambient primitive element.
residual_risks: The result is explicitly about the literal printed ambient-primitivity wording; an intended smaller-field meaning produces the repaired equivalence instead.

The audited result identifies the ambient-versus-subfield primitivity mismatch and gives a concrete proper-subfield counterexample; Resultary found only the assigned correction. Standard primitive-normal-basis theorems do not bridge this mismatch because primitivity is relative to the field whose multiplicative group is generated.
